title: Living with Garner and Doc West and recording "Pastel" at McGregor studio
summary: He recalls the shared place on 28th Street, Doc West's cooking, and how Ross Russell renamed his song, which became a hit in Honolulu.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: And we became very close friends ever after that. He and I and Doc West used to live in the same place, on 28th Street in South Los Angeles. Of course, we weren't making that much money then, but we used to share our pennies. Doc was the official cook for the group, and he could really make some delicious meals out of nothing, you know. He'd get a steak and chop it up, and make cornbread... Oh, he was just a wonderful cook, and we had a ball. That was how Erroll happened to record "Pastel." There was an old piano there, and I used to sit down and play it, and he'd say, "hey, I like that." So I played it for him a few times, and with his memory and his mind, after playing it twice, he knew it. So we'd get on...

Getting back to Ross Russell and the record dates at McGregor Studio on 8th and Western: We were almost to the end of the session, so Erroll said, "Hey, let's play this." It was called "Please Let Me Forget At the Time." So Ross decided he didn't like that title, so we renamed it "Pastel." And a lot of people thought Erroll wrote it, but at 20 years later I'm still telling people, "That's my song." But that was one of the highlights, and it was sort of a hit for Erroll. Because after that, I went to
Honolulu, and the record was very big in Hololulu, so naturally it didn't hurt me at all.
